**Status:** PROVED (machine-checked, axiom-clean). Formalization milestone extending THM-369.
**What:** Three Lean 4 / Mathlib lemmas added to `LonelyRunner.lean`, each `#print axioms`-clean (`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, no sorry, no project axiom): (1) `lonely_of_no_multiple` -- for EVERY n>0, if no speed is divisible by n then t=1/n is n-lonely (the n-gon-vertex witness, all-n unconditional fragment); (2) `lonely_two` -- full n=2 via t=1/(2a) through `far_iff_fract`; (3) `three_lonely_sieve_cover` -- n=3 holds if no speed div by 3 OR no speed div by 2, isolating in checked code the residual kernel (speeds entangled with 6 after gcd-reduction).
**S534 extension:** THM-388 adds `three_one_three_mul_lonely`, proving in Lean that every residual family `{1,3r}` has the explicit `3`-lonely witness `t=1/3+1/(9r)`. The theorem is axiom-clean and pushes the formalization beyond the pure denominator sieve.
**Honest boundary:** the residual n=3 kernel (some speed div 3 AND some div 2) is NOT yet formalized; it is closed on paper by S522o (center-grid 1-D pigeonhole) and S526 (mod-3 Legendre character sum, |SAFE|=1/9+(2/9)chi(a)chi(b)/(ab)). The Lean file now faithfully separates "proved by sieve" from "needs the hard character/grid bound".
**Predictions/next:** formalizing the 1-D equally-spaced-points pigeonhole (S522o) would close n=3 completely in Lean; the mod-3 Gauss-sum evaluation (S526) is the next rung; the higher-resonance bound shared by n>=4 and n=14 is the research-grade rung.
**See:** `07-reflections/lrc-lean-formalized-cases-all-n-and-n3-sieve-cover-s528.md`, `07-reflections/lrc-lean-small-residual-family-s534.md`, `04-computation/lean/TournamentH7/TournamentH7/LonelyRunner.lean`, THM-369, THM-386, THM-388, HYP-2004, HYP-2005.

## HYP-2007: regular-polygon outside/inside split organizes LRC; inside-diagonal (r>=3) debt is the obstruction, born at n=4 (oracle-2026-06-01-S529)
**Status:** SUPPORTED (computation + identities); reframes the LRC obstruction geometrically.
**What:** The maximally symmetric tournament is the regular-n-gon (rotational/QR) one. Its chords split by dihedral skip-shell: skip-1 = SIDES (outside) = Hamiltonian cycle = ranking/cut/base-path; skip>=2 = DIAGONALS (inside) = cyclic/tile/cycle space. Cyclotomic chord-product prod|1-w^k|=n (verified n=3..10) ties the threshold 1/n to the polygon's OWN nearest-neighbour gap; for prime n the inside balance is the Gauss sum |sum chi(k)w^k|=sqrt(n) (verified p=3..13). The covering measure |LONELY(v)| = sum over resonances (sum m_i v_i=0) of prod f-hat(m_i), graded by order r=#nonzero m_i: r=0 = (1-2/n)^{n-1} (outside/independence), r=2 = pairwise (= S526's Legendre 1/9+(2/9)chi(a)chi(b)/(ab) for n=3, reproduced exactly), r>=3 = INSIDE DEBT (deep diagonals = S526/S527 higher-resonance obstruction).
**Evidence (lrc_polygon_inside_outside_s529.py +.out):** every regular-polygon AP set (1..n-1) gives direct |LONELY|=0 EXACTLY at n=3,4,5 (outside+inside annihilate; the Gauss-sqrt(n) balance in measure form = the unique tight case). Inside debt (r>=3) is identically 0 for n=3 (triangle has NO diagonals; two speeds admit no 3-term resonance) and first switches on at n=4 (-0.081 AP) -- the geometric birth of the open case.
**Predictions:** LRC = "signed sum of inside-diagonal shell contributions >= -(1-2/n)^{n-1}, equality only at regular polygon"; reduces to Gauss/Kloosterman sqrt(n)-domination per dihedral shell. Prime n classical (Weil); composite/AP frontiers (n=14,16,18) hard because shells share moduli (cf S17 "if 15 were prime").
**See:** `07-reflections/polygon-outside-sides-inside-diagonals-and-lrc-resonance-debt-s529.md`, `04-computation/lrc_polygon_inside_outside_s529.py`, `05-knowledge/results/lrc_polygon_inside_outside_s529.out`, HYP-2004, HYP-2005, HYP-2006, THM-369, THM-386.

## HYP-2008: the apex (source-sink) arc closes the polygon, is the unique boundary tile, and is the LRC loneliness gap (oracle-2026-06-01-S530)
**Status:** SUPPORTED/PROVED combinatorially (verified n=3..8); refines HYP-2007/S529.
**What:** Refinement of S529 "outside = base path." The polygon boundary is a Hamiltonian CYCLE (n arcs); the base path is only n-1. The closing arc = the source-sink arc (vertex n top-of-ranking to vertex 1 bottom) = the apex tile (n,1), range x-y=n-1 (MAXIMAL tile, staircase apex). So OUTSIDE (n sides) = base path (n-1) + apex (1); INSIDE diagonals = all OTHER tiles = C(n-1,2)-1 = n(n-3)/2. The apex is (a) the UNIQUE tile on the boundary (cyclic skip 1; all others skip>=2 = interior diagonals); (b) the cut/cycle HINGE -- its fundamental cycle is the WHOLE n-gon (others span contiguous (x-y+1)-sub-polygons); (c) the reason n=3 has no inside debt (its ONLY tile IS the apex, on the boundary; inside born at n=4 with diagonals (3,1),(4,2)).
**LRC:** rooting the cyclic order at the observer, source=leader, sink=trailer, source-sink arc = largest wrap-around gap = the arc cut to linearize into the ranking path = the OBSERVER'S BRACKETING GAP. Observer-lonely <=> apex clears 1/n on both sides (a>=1/n,b>=1/n). The n circle-arcs (n-1 inter-runner = runner base-path + 1 observer-apex) sum to 1; loneliness decided entirely by the apex. Regular polygon: apex clears exactly 1/n (tight). LRC = "the source-sink (apex) arc can always be opened."
**Evidence (lrc_apex_arc_source_sink_s530.py +.out):** dictionary verified n=3..8 (apex always (n,1), range n-1, unique boundary tile, inside=n(n-3)/2, apex fund-cycle=n); lonely-time scans n=3,4,5 show apex-gap loneliness, AP=regular gives clearance exactly 1/n.
**Predictions:** track the DYNAMIC apex (bracketing runner-pair changes at wall-crossings) as an interval-exchange on the source-sink arc; bounded-ansatz (S514/S519) = "apex cannot stay below 1/n-clearance for a full lap."
**CONVERGENT (two oracle S530 sessions independently hit this).** The parallel S530 (`07-reflections/the-source-sink-arc-is-the-pivot-s530.md`, `source_sink_apex_arc_s530.py`) adds three further guises of the SAME arc: (d) flipping the apex on the transitive tournament gives the MAXIMAL single-tile jump H = 1 + 2^{n-2} (n=3..8: 3,5,9,17,33,65) = transitive's big SC neighbour on the principal line; (e) it is the #SCC switch between block-extremes -- transitive (#SCC=n, largest gap>1/2, semicircle) <-> strong (#SCC=1, largest gap<1/2, Moon), 0 mismatches n=4,5,6; (f) it selects the two LRC lonely regimes (observer-outside/semicircle vs observer-inside/wrap). Combined statement: one arc = boundary closer = staircase apex/hypotenuse = max H-jump 1+2^{n-2} = #SCC n<->1 switch = LRC observer loneliness gap.
**See:** `07-reflections/the-apex-arc-source-sink-closes-the-polygon-and-is-the-lrc-gap-s530.md` (this session: combinatorial dictionary + gap-sum verification), `07-reflections/the-source-sink-arc-is-the-pivot-s530.md` (parallel: H-jump / #SCC / regimes), `04-computation/lrc_apex_arc_source_sink_s530.py`, `04-computation/source_sink_apex_arc_s530.py`, `05-knowledge/results/lrc_apex_arc_source_sink_s530.out`, HYP-2007, HYP-2004, THM-374, THM-382, THM-386.

## HYP-2009: LRC is outside clasp-gap forcing plus hidden inside chord debt (codex-2026-06-01-S529)
**Status:** OPEN; exact channel audit and proof-language refinement of HYP-2001/HYP-2003.
**What:** A tournament is a binary relation on simplex edges, but LRC-realizable tournaments come from a stricter regular-polygon source: an outside cyclic gap necklace determines hidden inside chord orientations by consecutive gap sums and the half-turn threshold. The dihedral group acts on the outside necklace; inside arcs split into chord-length channels. For LRC, the observer is a clasp vertex, and source is the outside condition that both clasp-adjacent gaps are at least `1/n`; interior runner arcs are shadow data except at boundary walls where diameter/endpoint ties create compactified debt.
**Evidence:** `lrc_polygon_outside_inside_s529.py` audits clasp-deleted regular `n`-gons. At `n=14`, the AP wall has 14 outside gaps, 78 hidden runner chords, `D_14` channel inventory `12,12,12,12,12,12,6`, and 6 hidden diameter ties; the tie-resolved interior has score histogram `((5,6),(6,1),(7,6))`, `c3=85`, `H=2641713`. Tournament Analysis over `n=4..18` by hidden boundary burden is transitive.
**Predictions:** HYP-2003's "wall-only => AP" should be restated as: only the regular outside necklace can keep the clasp gap closed while its inside chord-channel debts remain dihedrally balanced. A proof of n=14 should force non-AP sweeps to open the outside clasp before they can circulate all hidden endpoint/diameter debt.

## HYP-2010: the apex applies recursively = modular decomposition; H is multiplicative over disjoint apex-modules (oracle-2026-06-01-S531)
**Status:** SUPPORTED (verified); the H-multiplicativity is a candidate THEOREM (proof sketch below).
**What:** Every tile (x,y) is the APEX of the sub-polygon on the contiguous rank-block [y,x], so S530's outside/inside split recurs at every scale. The recursion IS the tournament's MODULAR DECOMPOSITION tree (= recursive sub-ranking tree S520o = recursive triangulation). Three quantities respect it:
 (A) COMBINATORICS: the n-gon contains exactly (n-s+1) sub-polygons of size s (s=3..n), summing to C(n-1,2) tiles -- exact self-similarity.
 (B) H (directed Ham-path count = loneliness meter S26): single apex-flipped block of size s has H=1+2^{s-2} (verified ranges r=2..7 -> 3,5,9,17,33,65). DISJOINT apex-flipped blocks MULTIPLY: H(A+B)=H(A)*H(B) (3*3=9, 5*5=25, verified n=7,8,9) -- because flipped contiguous blocks are MODULES and the transitive quotient has H=1, so H(T)=prod_modules H(module). NESTED flips COUPLE (not multiplicative): concentric "diameter onion" (1,n),(2,n-1),... climbs toward the REGULAR tournament (=regular exactly at n=5, H=15; n=7->123; n=9->1479), endpoint-anchored chain stays low (n=7->31). The disjoint-multiply / nested-couple split is the quantitative form of S520o "arcs are not independent".
 (C) LRC: the feasible (loneliness) arc is carved recursively by runners (cascade S527); carve tree mirrors the sub-polygon tree; #components branches (1,2,4,4,2) then prunes; early shrink ~ (n-2)/n. REGULAR POLYGON carves the apex to EXACTLY 0 (tight); non-AP leaves positive surviving apex. LRC = "recursive carving never empties the observer's apex".
**Proof sketch (B, modular multiplicativity):** contracting each flipped contiguous block (module) to a point yields the transitive tournament (acyclic, H=1); directed Ham paths factor as (paths through quotient) x prod(internal module paths); quotient transitive => unique linear order => H(T)=prod H(module). Candidate THM.
**Predictions:** prove modular H-multiplicativity cleanly (THM); find the nested-coupling generating function along a chain; make the recursive carve rigorous via the three-gap (Steinhaus) theorem for per-runner sub-arc splits.
**See:** `07-reflections/the-apex-recursion-modular-tree-recursive-H-and-recursive-carving-s531.md`, `04-computation/recursive_apex_hierarchy_s531.py` (+.out), `04-computation/recursive_apex_H_law_s531b.py` (+.out), HYP-2008, HYP-2007, S520o, S527, THM-374, THM-382.

## HYP-2011: n=4 parity law -- odd-sum triples have zero inside debt (oracle-2026-06-01-S531)
**Status:** PARTIALLY-TRUE / THM-worthy for the odd-sum branch.
**What:** For n=4, the covering character `g_k=-sin(pi*k/2)/(pi*k)` is supported only on odd `k`. The order-3 inside-debt resonance therefore needs all odd harmonic indices, so reducing mod 2 gives the obstruction `a+b+c=0 mod 2`. Hence `a+b+c` odd implies the inside-debt term is identically zero, and `|SAFE|=1/8+pairwise>0`.
**Evidence:** `04-computation/lrc_n4_parity_inside_debt_s531.py` verifies 0 violations over 1336 primitive triples with speeds <=22; all 752 odd-sum triples have positive safe measure, min `1/18`; the even-sum core contains the unique tight AP `{1,2,3}` in the audited range.
**Predictions:** close the even-sum n=4 core by a mod-4 triple character sum; general n>=6 needs a multi-channel law because the character support has multiple residue classes.
**See:** `05-knowledge/hypotheses/HYP-2011-lrc-n4-parity-inside-debt-law.md`, `07-reflections/lrc-n4-parity-law-and-the-loneliness-ladder-s531.md`, `04-computation/lrc_n4_parity_inside_debt_s531.py`, `05-knowledge/results/lrc_n4_parity_inside_debt_s531.out`, HYP-2004, HYP-2007.

## HYP-2012: the LRC multi-channel metric is the independent-pair count floor(n/2) (oracle-2026-06-01-S532)
**Status:** PARTIALLY-TRUE; n=4 fixed-frame claim verified and n=14 CRT channel interpretation supported.
**What:** The multi-channel generalization should track both the amount and state of independent pairs: a maximum matching of disjoint arcs supplies `floor(n/2)` tournament channels, and LRC variants use the corresponding runner matching plus an apex singleton when the moving-runner count is odd. At n=4, with a suitable fixed frame, the two matching-arc bits index all four tournament isomorphism classes; from n=6 onward the obstruction is a joint state of several channels rather than a single parity bit.
**Evidence:** `independent_pairs_channels_s532.py` verifies the n=4 bijection for 8/16 frames, records `floor(n/2)` counts through n=14, and shows n=6 has full-support resonance in all 120 sampled primitive 5-sets. `lrc_independent_pairs_s532.py` identifies n=14 CRT pairs as a maximum runner matching plus apex singleton and decomposes AP resonance debt into within-channel, cross-channel, and higher-order pieces; its tile matching pass was corrected to exact matching so n=8 has 4 channels.
**Predictions:** compute n=6 inside debt as a function of the three-pair joint state; find the mod-6 analogue of the n=4 odd-sum parity law; characterize which n=4 fixed frames give the A000568(4) bijection.
**See:** `05-knowledge/hypotheses/HYP-2012-independent-pairs-multichannel.md`, `07-reflections/independent-pairs-are-the-channels-s532.md`, `04-computation/independent_pairs_channels_s532.py`, `04-computation/lrc_independent_pairs_s532.py`, HYP-2011, HYP-2008, HYP-2003.

## HYP-2013: independent pairs determine the iso class exactly iff n<=4; the coupling gap measures the multi-channel remainder (oracle-2026-06-01-S532b)
**Status:** SUPPORTED (verified n=3..8); complement to HYP-2012.
**What:** Flipping an arc-set S (rest fixed) can index all A000568(n) iso classes only if 2^|S| >= A000568(n). INDEPENDENT pairs (a matching) give |S|<=floor(n/2), so they alone determine the iso class iff 2^floor(n/2) >= A000568(n) -- TRUE (equality) iff n<=4. Define COUPLING GAP = ceil(log2 A000568(n)) - floor(n/2) = 0,0,2,3,6,9 for n=3..8 = the genuinely-coupled bits beyond the independent-pair channels. Verified n=5: best 2-arc matching over best frame reaches only 4 of 12 classes (the 2^2 ceiling). Channel gcd-decomposition: skip j -> gcd(n,j) cycles of length n/gcd(n,j); a PERFECT MATCHING (max independence) iff j=n/2 (diameter shell, even n only). n=4 = smallest even n with a diameter matching = the 2 diameters = the user's 2 independent pairs = where the inside is born (S529). Odd n has NO matching channel (all shells are odd cycles, coupled).
**Synthesis:** independent pairs = the FACTORING channels (S531: vertex-disjoint modules multiply H); coupling gap = the nested/shared-vertex obstruction = inside debt (S529) = nested coupling (S531). 'Amount/state of independent pairs' = free coordinate; the gap (>0 for n>=5) = the multi-channel difficulty, zero only n<=4.
**Predictions:** is the coupling gap an achievable bound (floor(n/2) independent + gap coupled arcs index all classes)? does the LRC inside-debt resonance order match the coupling-gap channel count?
**See:** `07-reflections/independent-pairs-determination-boundary-and-coupling-gap-s532b.md`, `04-computation/independent_pairs_boundary_s532b.py` (+.out), HYP-2012 (concurrent independent-pairs=channels), HYP-2010 (modular H), HYP-2007 (inside debt), opus-S524 (n=14 CRT).

## HYP-2014: almost-fixed frame coupling is the multi-channel breakdown (oracle-2026-06-01-S533)
**Status:** SUPPORTED (verified n=3..12 divisibility; clean-frame boundary audited).
**What:** `2^floor(n/2)` divides `A000568(n)` for n=3..12, giving a free pair-flip factor shadow on tournament isomorphism classes. But a clean fixed-frame factorization exists only for n<=4; at n=5 the required frames overlap, so flipping one independent pair changes how the others sit on the shared frame. This breakdown is the inter-pair coupling that makes the LRC multi-channel problem hard.
**Evidence:** `almost_fixed_frame_s533.py` proves the divisibility pattern in the audited range and shows clean fixed frames fail beyond n=4; `n6_inside_debt_three_channel_s533.py` supports the three-channel n=6 gate/apex picture.
**Predictions:** measure the coupling as deviation from the free `(Z/2)^floor(n/2)` product; relate the coupling measure to inside-debt resonance order and to the failure of single-congruence parity laws for n>=6.
**See:** `05-knowledge/hypotheses/HYP-2014-almost-fixed-frame-coupling.md`, `07-reflections/almost-fixed-frame-and-the-coupling-s533.md`, `04-computation/almost_fixed_frame_s533.py`, `04-computation/n6_inside_debt_three_channel_s533.py`, HYP-2012, HYP-2013.

## HYP-2015: n=14 diameter-channel state refines the independent-pair metric (codex-2026-06-01-S532)
**Status:** OPEN; K4 toy model and n=14 chord-channel inventory support the refinement.
**What:** HYP-2012 says independent pairs are the multi-channel metric; this refinement says n=14 needs the state and matching shape of those independent pairs under a fixed scaffold. In K4, a fixed scaffold `0->1->2->3` plus `0->3` and two free independent pair-arcs `(0,2),(1,3)` hits all four ordinary tournament isomorphism classes. In clasp-deleted n=14, the diameter channel has exactly six mutually independent hidden chords plus one singleton runner.
**Evidence:** `lrc_independent_pair_channels_s532.py` finds the K4 state table `00,01,10,11` gives the four classes with `(H,c3,SCC)` values `(5,2,(4)), (3,1,(3,1)), (3,1,(3,1)), (1,0,(1,1,1,1))`; 24/48 K4 independent-pair scaffolds are complete coordinates. In n=14, channels `d=1..6` have 12 edges, max matching 6, and 7 maximum matchings, while the diameter channel `d=7` has 6 edges, max matching 6, exactly 1 maximum matching, and all edges independent.
**Predictions:** a wall-only n=14 counterexample must carry a compatible state vector on the six diameter independent pairs; if that vector is not AP-balanced, the outside clasp opens or endpoint/resonance debt exports to a deeper labelled layer. "Wall-only => AP" should factor through a finite classifier of diameter-pair states under fixed non-diameter scaffold.

## HYP-2016: the mod-6 three-channel parity law for the n=6 inside debt (oracle-2026-06-01-S533c)
**Status:** VERIFIED (computation, n6_full_support_three_channel_law_s533b.py); generalizes the n=4 'a+b+c odd' parity law.
**What:** In the covering expansion |LONELY|=sum_{sum m_i v_i=0} prod ghat(m_i), the characters vanish iff n*|m where n*=n/2 (even n) or n (odd n). A full-support resonance (all n-1 runners) needs, mod n*, that 0 = sum u_i v_i for units u_i in (Z/n*)^x. 
 n=4 (n*=2, units {1}): one fixed sum -> debt-free iff sum v_i ODD = 'a+b+c odd' (ONE channel, no sign freedom).
 n=6 (n*=3, units {+-1}): a SIGN per runner -> debt-free iff NO eps in {+-1}^5 has sum eps_i v_i = 0 mod 3. THE FIRST genuinely multi-channel parity law. mod 6 = (mod-3 residue channel) (x) (mod-2 sign-unit). The 3 channels = residues mod 3 = the diameter/antipodal pairs (S530/S532).
**Reduction (verified):** inert runners (v=0 mod3) contribute 0; active runners (v!=0 mod3) contribute {1,2} mod3 freely; with k=#active the reachable sums mod3 = all of Z/3 iff k>=2, {1,2} iff k=1. So FULL-SUPPORT debt VANISHES iff k=1 (for primitive sets: exactly ONE runner !=0 mod3). Verified on curated sets ((3,6,9,12,1) etc. debt=0, zero resonances) and 400/401 random primitive 5-sets (1 miss = bounded-search integer-feasibility edge case).
**Value vs feasibility:** existence is mod 3; the debt VALUE/sign is graded by m mod 6 (|ghat(m)|=sqrt3/(2pi m), sign by m mod 6: 1,2->-, 4,5->+). 'Any-order' debt is almost always present (inert runners form a scaled 3*(...) sub-system with its own resonances = the S531 recursion); the CLEAN channel law is the full-support term, exactly as n=4's order>=3 IS full-support.
**Unified (all n):** full-support debt-free iff 0 not representable as sum (units mod n*) v_i; #channels = #residue classes, per-runner freedom = (Z/n*)^x. 'a+b+c odd' = the unit-trivial shadow; n=6 = first nontrivial unit group.
**Predictions:** n=8 (n*=4, units {1,3}) signed-by-{1,3} balance mod 4; n=9 (n*=9, units phi(9)=6) six-fold unit channel; tie integer-feasibility edge cases to the resonance lattice.
**See:** `07-reflections/n6-inside-debt-three-channel-parity-law-mod6-s533c.md`, `04-computation/n6_full_support_three_channel_law_s533b.py` (+.out), `04-computation/n6_inside_debt_three_channel_s533.py` (+.out), HYP-2007 (inside debt), HYP-2012/2013 (independent pairs=channels), HYP-2014/2015 (concurrent S533/S532), S531 (n=4 parity), S526 (mod-3 Legendre).

## HYP-2017: LRC n=18 attempt -- parity obstruction is VACUOUS at n*=9 (potent only at n=4); the prime-power degradation (oracle-2026-06-01-S534o)
**Status:** honest proof ATTEMPT (n=18 NOT proved); rigorous sub-cases + new parity-degradation finding.
**What:** n=18 (17 speeds, 1/18), n*=n/2=9=3^2. (1) RIGOROUS (THM-369 sieve): for every q<=18 with no speed divisible by q, t=1/q is 18-lonely (1/q>=1/18); verified 245/245 no-mult-of-9 sets lonely at t=1/9. A counterexample must be q-COVERED for all q in {2..18}. (2) NEW: the S533c parity law generalizes (full-support debt-free iff 0 not representable as sum c_i v_i mod n*, c_i in {1..n*-1}) and is VACUOUS at n=18: 0/3000 primitive 17-sets debt-free. Firing-rate degradation: n=4(n*=2,units{1}) ~60%; n=6(n*=3) ~3%; n>=8 0%. The parity obstruction is essentially UNIQUE to n=4 (trivial unit group). 3-adic reason: mod 9 nonzero residues split into units {1,2,4,5,7,8} (v3=0) and {3,6} (v3=1); a v3=1 runner can contribute 0 mod9 (c=3,6), a unit runner contributes all {1..8}; so any unit runner => 0 reachable => debt present. Debt-free needs ALL runners div by 3 => recurses to n=6 mod-3 law one 3-adic level down (non-primitive) = the prime-power recursion. (3) HEURISTIC: cascade threshold (n-1)((n-2)/n)^{n-2}=17*(8/9)^16=2.58>=1 passes (margins 1.12/2.04/2.31/2.58 for n=7/14/16/18); AP=regular-18gon carves to EXACTLY 0 (tight extremal), random primitive stays ~0.148; non-rigorous (Erdos-Turan discrepancy log factor).
**Verdict:** n=18 NOT proved. Wall = sieve-covered residual + discrepancy/coupling gap (same as n=14/16, general conjecture). Parity route now known insufficient beyond n=4.
**Predictions:** closing n=18 needs either (i) rigorous discrepancy bound for the cascade shrink on the sieve-covered residual, or (ii) coupled control of the order>=3 inside debt the parity bit cannot see.
**See:** `07-reflections/lrc-n18-proof-attempt-parity-vacuity-prime-power-s534o.md`, `04-computation/lrc_n18_proof_attempt_s534.py` (+.out), HYP-2016 (mod-6 three-channel parity), HYP-2007 (inside debt), HYP-2003 (n14 covering), S527 (cascade), THM-369 (sieve), S17.

## HYP-2018: LRC mapping spectrum -- restriction of realizable iso-classes = retained metric; the NEAR-GRAPH mapping is the sweet spot (oracle-2026-06-01-S535o)
**Status:** SUPPORTED (computed n=4,5,6); reframes LRC as membership on a restricted family.
**What:** The S518 order-tournament menu is non-restrictive (the conjecture hides in the walk) because a tournament keeps only ORDER; loneliness is METRIC (1/n). PRINCIPLE: the realizable iso-class set shrinks as the mapping retains more metric. Computed spectrum (R=realizable/all):
 - M0 order tournament: no restriction (walk).
 - M1 NEAR-GRAPH (i~j iff circular dist<1/n): realizable = circular indifference graphs; R=8/11,20/34,54/156=0.73,0.59,0.35 (SHRINKS with n). **Status:** SUPPORTED (verified); rigorous import of Tutte/Seymour flow theory into the resonance machinery.

**Verified (lrc_nowhere_zero_flow_s537.py):** (1) FACTORIZATION: inert runner (v_i=0 mod n*) = free edge, factor (n*-1)^#inert; active runner constrained; NZ-flow-count = (n*-1)^inert * C_active. (4) FLOW POLYNOMIAL: unit-weight dipole reproduces F(D_m;k)=((k-1)^m+(-1)^m(k-1))/k exactly; inside-debt VALUE = ghat-weighted NZ-integer-flow enumerator (=0 exactly when NZ-flow count=0), obeys deletion-contraction (= S531 recursion).

Flow<->coloring (Tutte) duality = the two faces of LRC; ties to circular chromatic/flow number.
**Honest limit:** reframes the inside-debt/parity layer (insufficient beyond n=4) into flow language; does NOT prove LRC; provides the toolbox.
**Predictions:** (i) full |LONELY| = flow enumerator over ALL sub-dipoles (runner subsets) of prod ghat -- a flow-polynomial sum with deletion-contraction; (ii) circular-flow-number bound via Tutte 5-flow/Seymour 6-flow; (iii) counterexample <=> a derived graph lacks a NZ flow of a prescribed circular type.

## HYP-2029: LRC pairwise structure is a T(R)IENERMENT (ties=nearness); loneliness=observer tie-degree 0; the Gabor uncertainty angle (oracle-2026-06-01-S539o)
**Status:** SUPPORTED (computed n=4,5,7); unifies the mapping program via the repo trienerment machinery.
**What:** The LRC pairwise comparator is a t(r)ienerment (3 states i->j, i<-j, i<->j=tie), NOT just a tournament. Edge {i,j}: strict TIE iff circular dist < 1/n (NEAR); else directed by half-turn. With strict ties dist < 1/n, globally tie-free states do occur, and are exactly regular n-gon wall states (including AP/unit-wall witnesses). **ONE-LINE:** local emptiness is guaranteed by FREQUENCY spread (decorrelation), not spatial; engine = the positive independence term (1-2/n)^{n-1}; mechanism = temporal-spread+rotation; sole obstruction = arithmetic frequency-concentration, maximal & exactly cancelling at the regular polygon. ## HYP-2040: LRC conditional-clearance cascades carry a hidden transitive wedge debt (codex-2026-06-01-S549)
**Status:** OPEN; exact tournament identity now THM-395, LRC lift still to be made proof-bearing.
**What:** Read the S548 cascade as `mu(F_m)=prod_k P_k`, where `P_k=P(runner k safe | previous runners safe)`, but attach a second ledger to each accepted clearance.  In any transitive tournament, an edge `X->Y` forbids every third vertex `Z` with `Z->X` and `Y->Z`; equivalently the backward wedge `Y->Z->X` cannot occur.  THM-395 proves the exact tournament ledger: for any tournament, `sum_{X->Y} |{Z: Z->X and Y->Z}| = 3*c_3(T)`, so the hidden fact is directed-triangle debt seen edge-locally.
**LRC reading:** Scalar clearances measure safe-set shrink, while backward-wedge exclusions measure the third-object dependence that a product formula must pay.  AP/regular rows should concentrate this wedge debt at the last runner or compact wall; non-AP rows should spread it across earlier factors, leaving positive open clearance.  The useful vertices are likely clearance obligations, endpoint owners, wall events, p-adic zero branches, or Gabor zero columns rather than raw runners.
**Assumption challenge:** runner-only and arc-only vertex choices were considered but are probably too lossy.  The preserved predicate is observer tie-degree zero / observer-source target / zero danger occupancy; exact gap lengths and arithmetic labels are destroyed unless retained as p-adic or Gabor decorations.
**Predictions:** endpoint-pressure counterexample cores must realize closed chains of wedge violations or peel; the S550 verifier now reports `P_k`, backward-wedge counts, directed cycles, SCCs, score histograms, and Hamiltonian-path counts for the exact tournament base layer.  HYP-2041 identifies the same ledger as no-return/resonance debt; HYP-2042 warns that the 3-cycle layer is necessary but not sufficient for the full LRC ladder.  The next lift should put these statistics on endpoint owners, wall events, or clearance obligations.

**What:** LRC cascade = product of conditional clearances: order runners (base-path/jersey, S542); F_k=F_{k-1} cap {||v_k t||>=1/n}; c_k=|F_k|/|F_{k-1}|; LRC <=> prod c_k>0. TWO transitivity facts: Fact1(completion) (X,Y)&(Y,Z)=>(X,Z) propagates clearances forward; Fact2(HIDDEN, no-return) (X,Y) arc => NOT((Z,X)&(Y,Z)) forbids the 3-cycle Z->X->Y->Z = no later runner cyclically re-blocks. VERIFIED 4000/4000: Fact1<=>Fact2<=>no-3-cycle (same transitivity).
**KEY COMPUTATION (lrc_cascade_conditional_clearance_noreturn_s545.py):** c_1=1-2/n exactly. The product DEFICIT below (1-2/n)^{n-1} is driven by the # of RETURN 3-cycles = small 3-term resonances m_a v_a+m_b v_b+m_c v_c=0. Generic speeds: few returns -> c_k ~ 1-2/n, product ~ (1-2/n)^{n-1} (clearances propagate). REGULAR POLYGON (AP): ALL triples resonant (4/4,10/10,20/20 returns) -> conditional clearances COLLAPSE (last c_k=0) -> product EXACTLY 0 (tight). Fibonacci 1,2,3,5,8,13 (each a+b=c a return) = resonance-rich -> big deficit.
**UNIFICATION:** Fact2 (no return) <=> no 3-term resonance <=> inside debt vanishes (S529/S533) <=> cascade product stays at (1-2/n)^{n-1}>0 <=> local emptiness (S544). The cascade needs BOTH: Fact1 builds the product forward, Fact2 prevents cyclic re-block. The returns (resonances) are the SOLE obstruction, MAXIMAL at the regular polygon.
**REFRAME:** LRC = 'no return wins' -- returns drive the lonely MEASURE to 0 at the regular polygon but conjecturally never empty the lonely SET.
**Predictions:** quantitative bound prod c_k >= (1-2/n)^{n-1} - f(#returns) (the wedge/return debt, codex HYP-2040); set-vs-measure gap at the all-triples-resonant regular polygon; higher-order returns (k-cycles = k-term resonances) = full inside debt.

**SYNTHESIS:** x=repeated+ climbs the ladder; LRC = 'does the level-2 repeated-addition orbit's apex gap clear 1/n?'; difficulty fixed by the rung the speeds' recursion sits on. Within N, x=repeated+ bridges the line and the trees (S547): each tree level is the line repeated.

## HYP-2051: doubled primes are the one-dyadic lift that lets prime cycles cross parity (codex-2026-06-01-S550)
**Status:** OPEN synthesis; exact parity/residue/cycle identities, explanatory and predictive role still to test.
**What:** A doubled prime `2p` is the minimal even object that still remembers a prime odd core: dyadic height `1`, odd core `p`.  Cycle reading: `C_{2p}` is the bipartite double cover of the odd prime cycle `C_p`, so `2p` is even enough to alternate on two sheets but still prime enough to avoid extra odd-core factorization.
**Goldbach/Lemoine bridge:** Even Goldbach is `N=p+q`, with parity `1+1=0`.  Lemoine/Levy for odd `N` is `N=p+2q`, with parity `1+0=1`; equivalently it is the diagonal ternary form `N=p+q+q`.  The doubled prime is the repeated-prime Goldbach atom `(q,q)` compressed into one even term.
**Residue wheel:** On the mod-6 prime wheel, `P={1,5}` and `2P={2,4}`.  Then `P+P={0,2,4}` covers even residue channels while `P+2P={1,3,5}` covers odd residue channels.  Thus Lemoine is the cross-sheet convolution of the prime necklace with its doubled image.
**Repo link:** In HYP-1984's `N=2^h*odd_core` grid, doubled primes are the clean first-even row over prime odd cores: `p --x*2--> 2p`.  They should be treated as parity lifts/rank-one seams, not generic composites.  HYP-2049 is the stronger recursion-bridge sibling: `2p=p+p=2*p` is where the additive Goldbach diagonal and multiplicative doubling bridge coincide.
**LRC boundary addendum:** In the n=4 character frame, doubled-prime legs are boundary-active but pairwise quiet: the dyadic move can destroy the all-odd `t=1/4` witness while even reduced cofactors remain `chi4`-silent in the pair ledger.  The next Tournament Analysis object should use bridge cells `(N,p,q)` for `N=p+2q`, with Goldbach cells as comparison, and report edge flips against the S513 add/multiply stack.
**See:** `05-knowledge/hypotheses/HYP-2051-doubled-primes-parity-lift.md`, `07-reflections/doubled-primes-as-parity-lift-s550.md`, HYP-2049, HYP-2044, HYP-1984, HYP-1994, HYP-1983, HYP-2040, THM-391.

## HYP-2052: the division-point sieve has no finite completeness threshold for LRC(n) (opus-2026-06-01-S551)
**Status:** PARTIALLY PROVED — negative direction RIGOROUS; positive conjecture OPEN.
**Rigorous (PROVED):** For any bound `Q`, the n-runner set with one speed `= lcm(2,...,Q)` (rest arbitrary distinct) is *sieve-blind up to Q*: that speed is `≡0 (mod q)` for every `q<=Q`, so it is in the danger band for every multiplier `a`, and there is NO division-point witness `a/q` (THM-369) with denominator `<= Q`. These blind sets are still lonely — verified exactly for n=14, `{lcm(2..Q)}∪{1..12}` at `Q=14,16,18,20,24` (blind up to Q, explicit witness `2/27` checked safe ⇒ unconditionally lonely). Hence the minimal witness denominator is UNBOUNDED over lonely sets and a **bounded-modulus sieve cannot prove LRC(n) for n>=8**. This is the converse-limitation of THM-369 and the sieve analogue of the S1/HYP-2039 "measure is trivially >=0" fact — both cheap certificates are provably too weak.
**Positive conjecture (OPEN) HYP-2052+:** the minimal witness denominator `q_min(V)` of a primitive n-set is within a small constant of the least `q` not killed by any speed (next prime power above the largest divisor-loaded `q`). Evidence: hardest min-witness-modulus = 34 (speeds<=60) and 35 (speeds<=300), both on fully-loaded sets; random/structured sets resolve at `q<=25`. If proved, bounds witnesses by speeds ⇒ a real (large) finite reduction.
**Tournament Analysis:** at a witness the runners sit in the safe band `[1/n,1-1/n]`; the half-turn runner tournament has #SCC in {1,13} (S525 confirmed, 284/300 single block) and the largest gap straddles the observer (93%) — a vanishing near-regular round slice of A000568(13); the tight AP = regular 13-gon rotational tournament at `t=1/14`.
**See:** `05-knowledge/hypotheses/HYP-2052-lrc-sieve-no-finite-completeness.md`, `07-reflections/lrc-n14-sieve-has-no-finite-completeness-witness-denominator-unbounded-s551.md`, `04-computation/lrc_n14_multiprime_sieve_s551.py` (+.out), `04-computation/lrc_n14_sieve_completeness_probe_s551.py` (+.out), `04-computation/lrc_n14_witness_tournament_s551.py` (+.out), THM-369, THM-360, HYP-2039, S525, S1.

## HYP-2053: rigorous sufficient condition for LRC -- resonance energy E(v) < (1-2/n)^{n-1}; reduction to the high-energy core (oracle-2026-06-01-S550o)
**Status:** SUPPORTED/PROGRESS (computed; rigorous modulo a tail bound). Covers ALL sampled sets; reduces LRC to a thin core.
**THE BOUND:** from the covering identity |LONELY(v)| = (1-2/n)^{n-1} + sum_{0!=m, sum m_i v_i=0} prod ghat(m_i) (S529), the triangle inequality gives |LONELY(v)| >= (1-2/n)^{n-1} - E(v), E(v)=sum_{0!=m,..} prod|ghat(m_i)|. So E(v) < (1-2/n)^{n-1} => |LONELY(v)|>0 => LRC(v). [major/minor-arc: main term = independence (S544), E = resonance correction.] Controlled by the MINIMAL RESONANCE LENGTH l(v)=min sum|m_i|.
**COMPUTED (lrc_resonance_energy_full_s550b.py):** bound |LONELY|>=main-E validated all cases. GENERIC sets: E=0.005-0.058 << main 0.13 (margin ~0.1) -> LRC PROVEN. AP/regular: E=0.30 (n=5), 0.42 (n=6) >> main (the order>=3 returns/inside-debt S545 push E over) -> high-energy core, |LONELY|=0. HARD-CORE SCAN: bound proves LRC for 120/120 (n=5) and 60/60 (n=6) random primitive sets; the failing core is the thin small-l/many-returns set led by the AP.
**CORRECTION of S550 first pass:** the PAIRWISE energy E2 alone is NOT sufficient -- AP has E2=0.122<main yet |LONELY|=0; the FULL E (incl order>=3 returns) is required and gives E_AP>=main.
**PROGRESS:** LRC reduced to the HIGH-ENERGY CORE (E>=main = small-minimal-resonance/many-returns sets); the AP extremal of the core IS lonely (sieve t=a/n, THM-369). Residual = core minus sieve-handled cases.
**LIMITS:** truncation tail not rigorously bounded (margin large, safe); does NOT settle the core, so does NOT prove n=14/16/18 (a counterexample would live in the core).
**Predictions:** prove the geometric tail bound sum_{|m|>M} prod|ghat| <= C r^M (-> clean theorem, formalizable on near_pair/sieve); characterize the core as a bounded set of small-l speed ratios (finite check per n?); for n=14 (prime n*=7, S546) test core = sieve/AP sets.

## HYP-2054: the VITALI wall -- measure vs set; the S550 measure bound is intrinsically blind to the measure-zero core; the sieve is the constructive bypass (oracle-2026-06-01-S551o)
**Status:** SYNTHESIS (diagnoses the S550 wall; redirects the attack on the core).
**THE VITALI POINT:** on R/Z, x~y iff x-y in Q; an AC-transversal V has countable congruent translates tiling the circle => V non-measurable. Lesson: MEASURE and SET-NONEMPTINESS are INDEPENDENT (a nonempty/full set can be measure-0 or non-measurable).
**THE LRC WALL:** LRC is a SET statement (L(v)={t: all ||v_i t||>=1/n} nonempty); S550 controls only measure(L)>=main-E -> proves nonemptiness WHEN measure>0 (decorrelated bulk, 180/180). At the HIGH-ENERGY CORE (regular polygon) measure(open L)=0 EXACTLY (verified n=5,6,7) but L closed = the n-gon vertices {k/n} (n points, measure 0, NONEMPTY); t=1/n is a witness. Measure assigns 0 to empty/n-points/boundary alike -> CANNOT see nonemptiness -> the measure bound is intrinsically BLIND to the core. No sharpening of a measure/circle-method argument resolves it.
**RESOLUTION:** LRC's core is NOT Vitali-pathological -- measure-0 but EXPLICITLY CONSTRUCTIBLE; the SIEVE (THM-369) exhibits the rational witness t=a/q (no AC) = a constructive choice of Q-coset reps. Two complementary tools partitioned along the Vitali boundary: measure (S550) for the positive-measure bulk, construction (sieve/three-gap-CF S548/apex S530) for the measure-zero core. ## HYP-2059: the LRC loneliness radius is r/s, pinned by a straddling pair (opus-2026-06-02-S557)
**Status:** PROVED (Pinch Lemma + r/s corollary; proof in reflection); naive N3 small-pinch target refuted by S558. Deductive (per user: exact moments/conditions, not sampling).
**Pinch Lemma:** for M(S)=max_t min_i||v_i t|| < 1/2, the max is attained at t* where two distinct runners a,b STRADDLE the observer: frac(v_a t*)=M, frac(v_b t*)=1-M. (max of min-of-tents = breakpoint with +slope binder left, -slope binder right; equal only at an apex ⇒ M=1/2.)
**Radius=r/s:** (v_a+v_b)t*≡0 ⇒ t*=m/(v_a+v_b), (v_a-v_b)t*≡2M, and M(S)=r/s with s=(v_a+v_b)/gcd(v_a,v_b) (reduced pair-sum), r≥1. Verified exactly 200/200 random + every critical config.
**Exact reformulation:** LRC(14) ⟺ every 13-set has a pair (a,b) and integer m with ||v_j·m/(v_a+v_b)|| ≥ 1/14 ∀j. Only times that matter: m/(v_a+v_b).
**Necessary/structure:** N1 counterexample ⇒ optimal binding pair reduced sum s≥15; N2 tight ⇒ s≡0 mod 14 (floor: s=14, straddlers satisfy (v_a+v_b)/gcd=14) — deductively yields the tight-witness lattice, subsumes the sieve's mult-of-14 (pair (1,13)) and the gap value 2/27 (apex-doubled pair, s=27,r=2). S558 refutes naive N3: some lonely 13-sets have no reduced-sum ≤14 pair whose pinch clears all others. Correct replacement: small-pinch failure is a shield-cover residual; THM-396 proves any single universal blocker for a small pair is a true sum-multiple shield, while finite non-shield blocker covers remain to classify.
**See:** `05-knowledge/hypotheses/HYP-2059-lrc-pinch-pair-radius.md`, `07-reflections/lrc-n14-the-exact-moments-pinch-pair-and-r-over-s-radius-s557.md`, `04-computation/lrc_n14_pinch_pair_radius_s557.py` (+.out), `01-canon/theorems/THM-396-lrc-n14-small-pinch-universal-blocker.md`, `05-knowledge/hypotheses/HYP-2061-lrc-n14-small-pinch-shield-residual.md`, `04-computation/lrc_n14_small_pinch_shield_s558.py` (+.out); HYP-2058, HYP-2055, HYP-2060, oracle-S552, THM-369.

## HYP-2061: the pinch-time pigeonhole for LRC@14 IS the denominator sieve; defeated by A1; the fine-regime salvage (oracle-2026-06-01-S555o)
<!-- ⚠ ID COLLISION (MISTAKE-053): the file HYP-2061-lrc-n14-small-pinch-shield-residual.md is owned by codex-S558 (below). This oracle-S555o pinch-pigeonhole entry (file-less) is the duplicate → reassign to HYP-2067 when next touched. -->

**Status:** proof ATTEMPT -> rigorous REDUCTION (pinch=sieve) + honest gap + salvage direction.
**PINCH:** for a pair (a,b), t=1/(a+b) puts a at a/(a+b), b at b/(a+b), symmetric about 1/2, both at distance min(a,b)/(a+b)>=1/(a+b). So a+b<=n => the pinch CLEARS THE PAIR (>=1/n). Verified for pairs summing to 14 at t=1/14 (dist a/14).
**THE REDUCTION:** a third runner w is far at t=1/(a+b) iff (a+b) does NOT divide w. So pinch t=1/(a+b) lonely <=> no runner divisible by a+b = the denominator sieve (THM-369) at q=a+b. The pinch-pigeonhole 'some pinch clears all' = 'some s<=n has no multiple' = NOT sieve-covered. Naive pigeonhole also fails: 11 other runners vs ~7 pinch times.
**SALVAGE (fine regime):** the lonely times live at fine denominators q>n (S18) where danger arcs genuinely thin (band width 2q/n). The user's 'thin danger arc' intuition is correct ONLY at q>n. The fine-regime pinch pigeonhole = the open core (= S550 measure / S552 7-gon windows / multiples-of-n* coupling). Rational pinch (q<=n)=sieve; fine pinch (q>n)=the conjecture.
**Predictions:** a fine-regime pinch pigeonhole over denominators q in (n,Cn] with thin-band bounds; tie to S552 windows near t=j/7; combine with #far>=n-2 (S553, only one band can cover a pinch).

## HYP-2062: the FINE PINCH = a local LP clearance; lonely times in the first spreading window (0,1/n); the wall = LP degeneracy (oracle-2026-06-01-S556o)

## HYP-2061: HYP-2060 reduces the small-pinch route to sum-multiple shields or blocker covers (codex-2026-06-02-S558)
**Status:** PROGRESS; THM-396 proved, full blocker-cover contradiction open.
**WHAT:** Trying to prove from HYP-2060 exposed the exact failure mode of HYP-2059's naive N3. For n=14, a small pair `(a,b)` with reduced sum `(a+b)/gcd(a,b)≤14` has pair-safe pinch residues `m/(a+b)`. THM-396 proves that if a third speed is dangerous at every such pair-safe residue, then `(a+b)` divides that third speed: universal blockers are real sum-multiple shields. The stronger collective statement is false: non-shield blockers can jointly cover all pair-safe residues. THM-397 adds that every collective non-shield cover must contain an endpoint-window blocker modulo `a+b`; in particular, actual pair sums `a+b≤14` cannot be collectively non-shield covered. The remaining proof route is an endpoint-ledger/blocker-cover classification plus a global compatibility argument with HYP-2060.
**EVIDENCE/COUNTERWEIGHTS:** Exact S558 checks verify THM-396 for 1816 pair types with `a+b≤500`. The collective obstruction appears already for pair `(3,12)` with blockers `[14,8,10,11,13]`. A checkable HYP-2060-proxy set `(1,2,9,26,110,153,166,170,178,190,192,196,201)` has no small-pinch witness but is lonely with `M=48/191`; its small-pair shields are explicit. Tournament Analysis uses small pair-cells as vertices and shows the proxy's pair-cell tournament is transitive with one Hamiltonian path, while the finite cover obstruction is not yet contradicted.

## HYP-2063: the k+1=2q polynomial-method obstruction is the apex zero-divisor q (opus-2026-06-02-S559)
**Status:** PARTIAL PROOF — reduction + apex obstruction + tight-tuple repair PROVED; residual characterised (iff); full 2q corrector FALSE. Progress on the literature's n=14 wall (the 2q analogue of Sungkawichai-Trakulthongchai Prop 4.1).
**Reduction Theorem (proved, 0 mismatches q=3,5,7,11):** ℤ_{2q}≅ℤ_2×ℤ_q; every unit mod 2q is odd ⇒ mod-2 part of s·v+r·(1,…,2q-1) is FORCED (≡v_i+i), mod-q free over ℤ_q^×. Corrector into {1,…,2q-2}^{2q-1} ⟺ ∃ s',r'∈ℤ_q^×: s'w_i+r'c_i≠f_i ∀i (w_i=v_i mod q, c_i=i mod q, f_i=0 if v_i+i even else q-1). The whole prime-vs-2q gap = loss of mod-2 freedom.
**Apex Obstruction (proved):** unique speed ≡0 mod q in {1,…,2q-1} is the apex q=(k+1)/2=n/2; its constraint is r'-free; for the tight tuple it is 0≠0 (unsatisfiable) ⇒ full corrector FALSE for the tight tuple. The apex = the zero-divisor where ℤ_{2q} stops being a field = localized cause of Prop 4.1's failure = the repo's apex/co-observer (S530/S547).
**Tight-tuple repair (proved):** apex is 1/2-safe at base t=s/(2q); excluding it, s=r=1 corrects all non-apex runners (→2i mod 2q ∈{2,…,2q-2}). So the hardest tuple (the paper's c=k+1 bottleneck) is handled analytically once the apex is set aside. Verified all q.
**Residual (iff, verified):** parity-matched v, apex excluded: un-correctable ⟺ ratios {-c_i/w_i} cover ℤ_q^×; tight tuple collapses ratios to {-1} (easiest); hard residual = ratio-spread tuples.
**Open:** clear residual via r/p freedom of t=s/(2q)+r/p; hand apex to pinch/shield route (HYP-2061,THM-396); transfers to all k+1=2·prime (n=10,14,22).
**See:** `05-knowledge/hypotheses/HYP-2063-lrc-2q-tight-tuple-apex-obstruction.md`, `07-reflections/lrc-2q-tight-tuple-analogue-the-apex-is-the-field-failure-s559.md`, `04-computation/lrc_2q_tight_tuple_analogue_s559.py` (+.out), results lrc_2q_{apex_repair,residual_characterization}_s559.out; HYP-2056, HYP-2059, HYP-2061, THM-369; arXiv:2604.23906.

## HYP-2064: improving the lonely-runner gap bound IN CASES -- the sieve gives the FULL conjecture g>=1/(k+1) off a thin near-AP core; Tao's general 1/(2k)+eps is operative only there (oracle-2026-06-02-S557o)
**Status:** PROGRESS (case-wise gap lower bounds; large improvement over Tao in the bulk; general constant not beaten).
**FRAME:** trivial g>=1/(2k) IS the first moment (E[#near]=2k*theta<1 iff theta<1/(2k)). Tao adds c*log k/(k^2(loglog k)^2) via danger-arc OVERLAPS. Not beaten generally here.
**CASE HIERARCHY (rigorous on g(v)=sup_t min_i ||v_i t||):** (C1) SIEVE at q* = least q in {2..k+1} dividing NO speed: at t=1/q*, ||v_i/q*||>=1/q*, so g>=1/q*; if NOT sieve-covered then q*<=k+1 so **g>=1/(k+1), the FULL CONJECTURE**. (C2) all-odd -> g>=1/2. (C3) no mult of k+1 -> g>=1/(k+1) exactly. (C4) no mult of 2 or 3 -> g>=1/2.
**COMPUTED (lrc_gap_lower_bounds_by_case_s557.py, n=14):** 38/40 random primitive 13-sets NOT sieve-covered -> g>=1/14 proven (actual gaps 0.15-0.29, ~2-4x Tao's 1/26). all-odd g=1/2; no-mult-of-14 g=1/14 exactly; AP (wall) g=1/14 exactly (SATURATES conjecture -> no general bound can exceed 1/(k+1), Tao lives strictly below). KEY NUANCE: the 2 sieve-covered sets still have g=0.16, 0.23 -- sieve-covered != near wall; the genuinely hard locus is the even thinner near-AP slice.
**VERDICT:** 'improve in certain cases' = PROVEN: g>=1/(k+1) for ALL non-sieve-covered sets (the bulk), a large improvement over Tao there; structured cases reach 1/2. Tao's general bound is operative ONLY on the sieve-covered set, and the truly extremal gap (->1/(k+1)) only on its near-AP slice. On that core the repo's tools point the rest of the way: theta-deformed measure bound (S550: g>=theta when E(v)<(1-2theta)^k) and the local LP (S556).
**Predictions:** (1) theta-deformed measure bound -- largest theta<1/n with E(v)<(1-2theta)^k over the sieve-covered core gives explicit g>=theta there; (2) bound below the AP-distance of small-gap sieve-covered sets; (3) sieve (q<=n) + one fine pinch (q>n, S556) covers sieve-covered non-AP sets.
**See:** `07-reflections/improving-the-gap-bound-in-cases-the-sieve-gives-the-full-conjecture-off-a-thin-core-s557o.md`, `04-computation/lrc_gap_lower_bounds_by_case_s557.py` (+.out), THM-369 (sieve=t=1/q* bound), S554 (A1 sieve-covered), S550, S553, S556, S551.

## HYP-2064: A000568 is computed EXACTLY for all n by a float-free Burnside sum over odd partitions (monad-researcher-2026-06-02-S560)
**Status:** CONFIRMED (exact, verified n=1..20 against OEIS + repo CRT/series; extended n=21..50).
**WHAT:** The number of non-isomorphic tournaments A000568 equals the exact rational sum
  T(n) = sum_{partitions of n into ODD parts} 2^t / prod_j ( j^{m_j} * m_j! ),
where for a cycle type with (odd) cycle lengths c_1,...,c_k,
  t = sum_i (c_i-1)/2  +  sum_{i<j} gcd(c_i,c_j)
is the number of orbits of unordered vertex-pairs (Davis 1954 / Burnside; only all-odd cycle types fix any tournament). Accumulated with Python `Fraction`; the total is always an integer (asserted). NO floating point anywhere, so every value is provably exact and fast (sub-0.15s through n=50).
**WHY IT MATTERS:** the prior repo "exact" routine `a000568_asymptotic_exact_s26.py` is a float approximation+correction scheme that SELF-REPORTS failure from n=14 onward: it returns a(14)=28401423719122300 (off by 4; true 28401423719122304) and a(15)=...168256 (off by 1408; true ...166848), and it OverflowErrors at large n converting Fraction->float. The new `a000568_exact_burnside.py` returns the correct integers and never touches floats.
**VERIFIED:** a(1..20) match OEIS and the repo's independent CRT/series/gmpy2 computations exactly (a(20)=645022068557873570931850526424042500096, triple-confirmed: this script, a000568_series_exact_s26, a000568_n20_verified.txt). New guaranteed-exact extension a(21)..a(50) recorded in the output.
**See:** `04-computation/a000568_exact_burnside.py` (+ `05-knowledge/results/a000568_exact_burnside.out`); contrast `04-computation/a000568_asymptotic_exact_s26.py`; CLAUDE.md "Burnside: Fix(sigma)=0 for even cycles, 2^{orbit-pairs} for all-odd (A000568 exact through n=10)" — now verified exact and extended to n=50.

**EXTENSION (same session, second script `sc_vmerged_exact_burnside_s560.py`):** the SAME float-free Burnside machinery computes the full THM-283 mirror triple A000568 / SC / V_merged exactly, RECOVERING the lost q-deformed script (only its stale output `sc_a000568_q_deformed.out` to n=30 survived) and extending all three to n=60. Two canon identities re-verified with fresh exact arithmetic:
  (I) THM-283 mirror — A000568 = sum over all-odd cycle types of 2^c/z; SC = sum over cycle types with parts ≡2 mod 4 (+ one fixed point iff n odd) of 2^c/z; V_merged=(A000568+SC)/2 is an exact integer for all n. KEY: the inside-cycle pair-orbit term must be floor(L/2), which equals (L-1)/2 only for ODD L; the A000568 script's `(L-1)//2` is correct there but the SC even parts require floor(L/2). The new script uses L//2 universally.
  (II) MISTAKE-049 corrected framing — SC(2m) = A(m,4) where A(m,q)=sum_{odd λ⊢m} q^c/z is the q-deformed tournament count (A(m,2)=A000568(m)). This is exactly base-4 Burnside over odd partitions; verified SC(2m)==A(m,4) for m=1..25 (0 mismatches) and the sanity A(m,2)==A000568(m) for m=1..20.
  All SC values reproduced against THM-283 / `anti_aut_edge_merge_s189.out` (SC(2..19)). V_merged(3..30) reproduces `sc_a000568_q_deformed.out` exactly.
  **NOTE (ID hygiene):** HYP-2064 is a 3-way same-day collision (oracle-S557o gap-bound, codex-S560 gate-skip, this entry) — flagged per MISTAKE-052 for a future QC renumber; the three are distinct results sharing a number only by concurrency.
**See also:** `04-computation/sc_vmerged_exact_burnside_s560.py` (+ `05-knowledge/results/sc_vmerged_exact_burnside_s560.out`); THM-283, MISTAKE-049.
**See:** `05-knowledge/hypotheses/HYP-2064-lrc-n17-prime-gate-skip8.md`, `04-computation/lrc_n17_prime_gate_attempt_s559.py` (+.out), `07-reflections/lrc-n17-prime-gate-skip8-s559.md`; THM-369, HYP-1840.

## HYP-2065: LRC@14 even-fold MEASURE reduction -- lonely <=> the o odd danger arcs miss the (free, positive-measure) even-good set G; union bound and anti-correlation both REFUTED (oracle-2026-06-02-S558o)
**Status:** PROGRESS (correct new reduction synthesizing the concurrent agents; two natural levers ruled out -- dead-end documentation).
**SYNTHESIS:** the concurrent LRC@14 frontier converges on the APEX (mult of 14 = mod-7 singleton, opus-S552o = ZZ_14 zero-divisor, opus-S559 = even member a counterexample must contain, opus-S556 ThmB). The even-fold (opus-S554/S558, with LRC(13) PROVEN) says the even runners are always protected -> the whole difficulty is the ODD runners.
**THE REDUCTION:** split S into e even + o=13-e odd (e<=12 primitive). even v=2u: ||v t||=||u(2t)||; fold={v/2}. PROVEN LRC(13) => max g_fold(2t)>=1/(e+1)>1/14, so dropping threshold to 1/14 opens a positive-width window: the even-good set G={t: every even v >=1/14} has |G|>0 FOR FREE. Then **S lonely <=> |G \ U_{odd} D_v|>0** (D_v={||v t||<1/14}, |D_v|=1/7). SUF: |G|>o/7.
**COMPUTED (lrc_n14_evenfold_measure_s558.py, n=14, grid 6e5):** reduction exact. AP (|G|=0.457), V* (|G|=0.441) have safe slack=0 (the wall, S551); 12 random + 6 apex-forced all lonely, safe slack 0.10-0.17 (min 0.104). **Union bound |G|>o/7 FAILS 0/18** (odd danger o/7~0.43-1.29 always > |G|~0.20-0.53) -- pure counting of odd arcs is hopeless (= the 2-2/n>1 failure localized to the odd half). **Anti-correlation REFUTED:** at AP/V* the odd-danger density INSIDE G is 1.00 vs global 0.76 -- the odds CONCENTRATE in the even-good window at the wall; near-AP apex set {1..11,13,14} density-in-G=0.97, slack only 0.012.
**VERDICT:** clean reduction (|G|>0 free; LRC@14 <=> odd arcs miss G), boundary = exactly AP/V*. Both measure-counting levers fail; the real lever must be POSITIONAL (where the odd arcs sit in G -- pinch times opus-S557, or mod-7 phases opus-S552o), not their total length. Near-AP apex sets are the thinnest lonely configs (slack ~0.012) -- sharpens opus-S556's tension (apex keeps near-AP lonely by a hair, not robustly loose).
**Predictions:** (1) positional bound -- pinch times m/(v_a+v_b) restricted to G; (2) characterize when D_odd covers G (= AP-phase alignment); (3) quantitative |G| from fold collar (window width ~(1/(e+1)-1/14)/max-fold) then which odd phase-patterns cover that width.
**See:** `07-reflections/lrc-n14-the-even-fold-measure-reduction-do-the-odds-cover-the-even-good-set-s558o.md`, `04-computation/lrc_n14_evenfold_measure_s558.py` (+.out); opus-S554/S558 (even-fold/LRC(13)), opus-S552o (mod-7 singleton=apex), opus-S559 (zero-divisor), opus-S556 (mult-14 necessary+tension), opus-S557 (pinch), S550/S553/S551/S556o.

## HYP-2066: the user's A+B=C tournament IS the SUMMAND GRAPH; node C = the LRC pinch denominator; addition-shadow=pinch, multiplication-shadow=sieve, equal on the rationals (oracle-2026-06-02-S559o)
**Status:** SYNTHESIS / new cross-link (surfaced prior work + recorded an unrecorded bridge; not a new theorem).
**THE CONSTRUCTION = SUMMAND GRAPH (oracle-2026-05-03, summand-graph-fermat-zeckendorf.md):** digraph on N, a->n and b->n iff a+b=n (a!=b). Node n incoming-pair-count = floor((n-1)/2), parity-split (odd n: (n-1)/2; even n: n/2-1, midpoint pair excluded). Sec 4: summand graph IS the tournament staircase (node n <-> delta_{n-2}, depth-k mult 2^{k-2}, H on Zeckendorf, forbidden {7,21}).
**NEW BRIDGE:** opus-S557 pinch radius M=r/s, s=(v_a+v_b)/gcd = reduced PAIR-SUM, at t*=m/(v_a+v_b); oracle-S555o pinch pigeonhole over the floor(n/2) pairs summing to n = EXACTLY the incoming pairs of summand-graph node n. So **node C = LRC pinch denominator s=a+b; incoming pairs = pinch-pairs; pair-count floor((C-1)/2) = #pinch times at denom C.** Even C loses the midpoint pinch (apex pair C/2+C/2) = the apex/zero-divisor obstructing n=14=2*7 (HYP-2063).
**ADDITION vs MULTIPLICATION (codex-S365 + THM-369):** additive two-input shadow a->z,b->z iff a+b=z collapses to the TRANSITIVE tournament (x->z iff x<z) = the PINCH family; multiplicative shadow xy=z collapses to the DIVISIBILITY DAG (x->z iff x|z) = the SIEVE (THM-369: t=1/q lonely iff no speed div by q). oracle-S555o proved the rational pinch IS the sieve => **addition-shadow and multiplication-shadow COINCIDE on the rationals**; the FINE pinch (q>n, S556o) is where addition outruns divisibility = the open core. Same +/x spine as S548 hyperoperation tower (prod c_i=exp(-sum log c_i), log welds them).
**PARITY:** pair-count parity = pinch-count parity (even C drops apex pair); Burnside even-cycle fixes 0 / all-odd fixes 2^pairs; doubled prime 2q = parity-completion of prime additive basis (S546o); 14=2*7 hinge; even-fold (HYP-2065) = x2 on the summand structure.
**Predictions/next:** (1) use summand-graph incoming-pair lattice of fine denominators q in (n,Cn] to index the FINE-REGIME pinch pigeonhole (S555o handoff -- the additive shadow is the right index set); (2) restate HYP-2063 apex zero-divisor as 'even node's missing midpoint pair'; (3) Zeckendorf/Lucas summand chains (oracle-2026-05-05) as a sparse pinch family.
**See:** `07-reflections/the-summand-graph-node-is-the-lrc-pinch-denominator-addition-and-multiplication-shadows-s559o.md`; summand-graph-fermat-zeckendorf.md, lucas-summand-graph-zeckendorf-geometry.md, natural-operation-digraphs-and-product-sum-s365.md, multiplication-is-repeated-addition-...-s548.md, THM-369, HYP-2063, HYP-2065, S555o, S557, S546o.

## HYP-2067: geometry of the SUMMAND (antidiagonals) vs MULTIPLICAND (hyperbolas) graphs; the AP is their JOINT EXTREMUM = the LRC wall; sumset excess correlates +0.78 with looseness (oracle-2026-06-02-S560o)
**Status:** PROGRESS (geometric account + verified correlation; the Freiman<->LRC link is new, not yet a theorem).
**TWO FOLIATIONS:** summand graph (a,b->a+b) level sets = ANTIDIAGONALS x+y=n (in-pair count floor((n-1)/2), dense/additive, simple shadow=transitive tournament). Multiplicand graph (a,b->ab) level sets = HYPERBOLAS xy=n (in-pair count (tau(n)-[sq])/2, sparse/multiplicative, primes are sources, simple shadow=divisibility DAG). LOG BRIDGE: (x,y)->(log x,log y) sends xy=n to log x+log y=log n -- multiplicand = summand in log-coords (the +/x weld, S548).
**LRC DICTIONARY (S555o/S557):** pinch denominator C=v_a+v_b is a summand node; available denominators = the SUMSET S+S; runner w cleared at t=m/C iff C does NOT divide w = multiplicand/divisibility test (sieve THM-369). S555o (rational pinch=sieve) => the two foliations COINCIDE on integer points; the FINE pinch (C>n) = where addition outruns division = open core.
**AP = JOINT EXTREMUM (the why of the wall):** ADDITIVE -- distinct-pair sumset |S^+S|>=2k-3, equality IFF arithmetic progression (Freiman); AP minimizes pinch denominators = tightest pigeonhole. MULTIPLICATIVE -- AP {1..13} has a multiple of every q<=13 (max coverage), escaping the sieve only at q=n=14. So the AP is simultaneously sumset-minimal and coverage-maximal.
**COMPUTED (lrc_summand_multiplicand_geometry_s560.py, n=14, grid 2e5):** AP attains |S^+S|=23=2*13-3 (excess 0); random primitive 13-sets have 52-64 (excess 27-41). **CORRELATION(sumset excess, margin M) = +0.775** -- bigger sumset => looser (more pinch denominators=more room). AP is the tightest (M=1/14) and the unique sumset minimizer. V* excess=11 (tight by other means). Multiplicand in-degrees: 7,13 prime -> 1 pair; 24,30,36 -> 4; vs summand 11,14,17.
**SIMPLIFICATION:** index the pinch search by the SUMSET (addition supplies times), test clearance by DIVISIBILITY (multiplication); they meet on coarse rationals, work lives on the FINE sumset S+S cap (n,2max]. Freiman gives a quantitative surplus of pinch denominators off the AP (3k-4 first jump). ## HYP-2075: the LRC multi-sieve — pair-sum moduli are the complete, apex-free primitive (opus-2026-06-02-S562)
**Status:** METHOD/SYNTHESIS — multi-sieve implemented & measured; three assumptions challenged with data.
Three sub-sieves: (D) division t=a/m m∈{2..M}; (P) PINCH t=a/(v_i+v_j) pair-sum moduli (S557); (F) recursive even-fold (n=14→n=7→…). Composition over 329 random+loaded n=14 configs: div{2..14} 88.8%, fold 86.0%, div∪fold 95.1%, **PINCH 100% (complete)**.
**ASSUMPTION #1 (apex is a hard obstruction) — FALSE:** of 2366 configs with a multiple of 14, caught by m=14 alone 0%, by some m∈{2..13} **91%**. The apex is single-modulus; multi-sieve has NO apex (the S559/S561 apex was an artifact of the single-corrector mechanism, not loneliness).
**ASSUMPTION #2 (small-integer moduli) — wrong scale:** division incomplete at any finite M (S551; residual min-modulus 23+ unbounded), but pinch (pair-sum moduli) COMPLETE with bounded COUNT O(k²) and no apex. The natural LRC sieve moduli are v_i+v_j, not {1..M} nor the c=(k+1) lift.
**ASSUMPTION #3 (flat sieve) — recurses:** the 2-adic even-fold catches 86%; its only miss is the odd-split residual (S554), covered by pinch; bottoms out at all-odd (t=½).
**PROPOSAL:** sieve at PAIR-SUM RESIDUES mod p (t≡a/((v_i+v_j) mod p)) instead of/alongside the c=(k+1) base lift — optimal witness lives there, count O(k²), no apex; recurse 2-adically to proven LRC(13). HONEST: exact witness-finders on samples, not end-to-end; "pinch complete"=computes M(S); not a proof of LRC(14).
**SCALE-UP + REFINEMENT (monad-compute-2026-06-02):** stress-tested pinch completeness at ~60× scale, integer arithmetic, vs exhaustive ground-truth witness search. **20072 distinct n=14 configs, 0 pinch misses** (7968 broad incl. apex/LCM-loaded/random≤1000, QMAX=400; + 12104 dense near-AP scarce-witness configs incl. all single-coord AP perturbations, QMAX=600). Corroborates completeness far beyond 329. **REFINES the "optimal witness is a pair-sum" gloss (S557):** the *minimal-denominator* witness is frequently NOT a pair-sum — often a small division modulus (q=4,6,7,8,10,12) strictly smaller than any pair-sum. Pinch finds *a* witness (complete, apex-free) but not the smallest-q one. Every dense config had a witness with q≤26.
**COMPLETENESS EXTENDS TO n=15,16,17 (monad-compute-2026-06-02 follow-up):** same integer pinch-vs-ground-truth test, parameterized N (n-1 runners, threshold 1/n), QMAX=600. **n=15: 6528/6528; n=16: 6621/6621; n=17: 6676/6676 — 100% each, 0 refutations, 0 witness-less.** Combined 19,825 configs across n=15..17, 0 pinch misses; with n=14 that is ~39,900 configs at n=14..17 all caught. AP 1..(n-1) caught by the n-clock t=1/n at every n; minimal-denominator witness still often a small division modulus, not a pair-sum. Pair-sum moduli are a complete apex-free witness family across a range of n (sample-based, not end-to-end).
**See:** `05-knowledge/hypotheses/HYP-2075-lrc-multi-sieve-pinch-no-apex.md`, `07-reflections/lrc-multi-sieve-recursive-pinch-moduli-no-apex-s562.md`, `04-computation/lrc_multi_sieve_recursive_s562.py` (+.out); monad-compute: `04-computation/lrc_pinch_completeness_stress_s_monad_compute.py` (+.out), `04-computation/lrc_pinch_dense_adversarial_s_monad_compute.py` (+.out), `04-computation/lrc_pinch_completeness_n15_17_s_monad_compute.py` (+.out); HYP-2072, HYP-2059, HYP-2056, THM-369; S551, S557.

## HYP-2078: anti-automorphism Burnside extends to self-converse oriented graphs (A005639) and digraphs (A002499) (monad-researcher-2026-06-02-S565)
**Status:** CONFIRMED — one mechanical per-orbit-monodromy Burnside engine reproduces all six sequences exactly, brute-force ground-truthed; also resolves the repo's flagged A001174 bug.
**WHAT:** Generalizes the self-converse *tournament* engine (THM-283; SC=A002785, S560/S561/S562) to the other two orientation-reversal families. A "converse" reverses every arc = the involution iota swapping ->/<- (fixing none/both). For a representative permutation g of each cycle type, each orbit of unordered pairs contributes (#colors fixed by its monodromy); monodromy parity is `swap` (does g^L swap the pair's endpoints) for the iso count and `swap XOR (L mod 2)` for the self-converse count. Color models: tournament (C=2,Cfix=0), oriented graph (C=3,Cfix=1: {none,->,<-}), digraph (C=4,Cfix=2: {none,->,<-,both}).
**VERIFIED:** independent brute-force orbit enumeration matches the engine for all three families (tournaments/oriented n<=5, digraphs n<=4; 0 mismatches). Engine == OEIS: A000568 & A002785 (n<=14), A001174 & A005639 & A002499 (n<=40, official Robinson/Howroyd/Harary-Palmer b-files), A000273 (n<=9). The two self-converse families are the classical A005639 (Robinson 1976, oriented) and A002499 (Harary-Palmer 1966, digraphs) — the S561 handoff guesses confirmed.
**BONUS:** gives the CORRECT A001174(8)=575016219 (matches OEIS to n=40), resolving the "off by 3247 at n=8" bug flagged in burnside_unified_s28.py. The old closed formula used 3^{#pair-orbits}; an orientation-reversing pair-orbit can only take the iota-fixed color (none), which the per-orbit Cfix branch handles correctly.
**HONEST:** verification + repo gap-fill, NOT OEIS extension (Howroyd b-files reach n=50 via efficient formulas; the orbit-walk engine is O(p(n))).

**INTERPRETATION:** time should be collapsed to a finite active-set catalogue plus a finite dual obstruction ledger. Tightness is an arithmetic `n`-clock / CRT-gear stratum; generic rows clear by pair-pinch; true failure should have to export a nonempty labelled endpoint core.

## HYP-2083: the `2n-1` antipodal witness reduction is the summand graph acted on by multiplicative units (codex-2026-06-03-S571)
**Status:** SUPPORTED by structural synthesis + S571 audit.
**WHAT:** At `C=2n-1`, the S553 witness family is the summand graph node `C` with `(Z/CZ)^*` acting on incoming pairs. Summand pair `{a,C-a}` = antipodal shell; missed unit shell = invertible witness clock `a^{-1}/C`; missed nonunit shell = composite-modulus blind spot; AP = all-lower transversal. Addition creates the shells, multiplication by units makes them visible.
**EVIDENCE (`lrc_antipodal_summand_units_s571.py`):** prime `C=11,13` has every shell unit-visible in one orbit; composite `C=15` splits into unit/gcd-3/gcd-5 strata and the n=8 sporadics miss only nonunit shells; composite `C=27` splits into unit/gcd-3/gcd-9 strata and n=14 `V*={1..11,13,24}` misses nonunit `{12,15}` while doubling `{3,24}`. Follow-on `lrc_second_gap_transversal_audit_s572.py`: in bounded primitive boxes through `k=6`, every row below `2/(2n-1)` is already `n`-clock tight with `M=1/n` and is a perfect antipodal transversal; bounded flip-set menu is AP plus the known `{2}` sporadics.
**ODD/EVEN:** odd `C` has no midpoint, so summand pairs are exactly cyclic antipodal pairs. Even `C` has fixed midpoint `C/2=-C/2`, and the distinct-summand graph excludes the degenerate midpoint pair; this is the LRC apex/half-turn shape.
**HONEST:** structural bridge, not a spectral-gap proof. The next theorem branch is to close the nonunit-hole branch by a second clock, modulus lift, or gcd-stratum descent.
**See:** `05-knowledge/hypotheses/HYP-2083-lrc-antipodal-summand-unit-bridge.md`, `07-reflections/lrc-2n-minus-1-summand-unit-bridge-s571.md`, `04-computation/lrc_antipodal_summand_units_s571.py` (+.out), `04-computation/lrc_second_gap_transversal_audit_s572.py` (+.out); HYP-2052, HYP-2055, HYP-2059, HYP-2075.

## HYP-2085: finite time Burnside must use the lonely-word stabilizer; Fourier modes expose clock families (codex-2026-06-03-S571)
**Status:** PROGRESS; finite quotient diagnostic built, proof use open.
**WHAT:** Discretises LRC time to `Z/N` and audits the proposed Burnside/Fourier model. The full cyclic group acts on ambient slots but usually not on the lonely subset `X`, so `|X|/N` is density, not a valid full-group orbit count. The legal finite Burnside group is `K=Stab(1_X)`, the stabilizer of the whole lonely time word; then `|X/K|=|X|/|K|`. Fourier transform of `1_X` is the representation-theoretic dual.
**EVIDENCE (`lrc_time_burnside_fourier_s571.py`, `N=38640`):** audited n=14 rows have trivial binary-word stabilizer, so the full-shift quotient gives no structure beyond density. AP/V* have only 6 lonely slots (`1/6440` density); non-wall rows range from `1/140` to about `0.1285`. Fourier modes still expose clock families: near-AP uses `6,12`; S562 n14 packet uses `21,42`; dyadic lift uses `42,84`; no-small-pinch proxy uses `2,24`; random low-resonance uses `34,2`.
**INTERPRETATION:** primitive integer reset length is constant, so classify by finite time word: period/stabilizer and Fourier support. Since the binary stabilizer is usually trivial, meaningful Burnside should move to owner-labelled event words from S564/S570: runner owner, pair-sum denominator, `G` component, wall endpoint, endpoint core.
**Tournament Analysis:** vertices were speed-set time words; observable `(density, stabilizer, Fourier entropy/top mode, period)`; switch harder = lower density, more folding, lower entropy/stronger top mode. Fingerprint transitive with no directed 3-cycles and one Hamiltonian path.
**See:** `05-knowledge/hypotheses/HYP-2085-lrc-finite-time-burnside-fourier.md`, `04-computation/lrc_time_burnside_fourier_s571.py` (+.out), `07-reflections/lrc-time-burnside-fourier-quotient-s571.md`; HYP-2080, HYP-2081, HYP-2082, HYP-2077, HYP-2075.

**Status:** SUPPORTED by finite dihedral audit; proof use open.

The all-odd probe shows the fixed-point term: `5845` lonely slots plus one reflection-fixed half-turn gives `2923` dihedral orbits. Every audited row has odd-sector L2 `0.000e+00`; imaginary Fourier mass is numerical roundoff only.
**INTERPRETATION:** HYP-2086 puts the hard regime on the Burnside fixed boundary; HYP-2087 says the time-word obstruction is already confined to the dihedral reflection-fixed/cosine sector. The next labelled-event audit should test which runner-owner, pair-sum, wall-endpoint, and endpoint-core labels remain fixed by reflection, and which symmetries appear only after labels are forgotten.

## HYP-2088: strict sub-edge LRC rows must satisfy a three-clock blocker ledger (codex-2026-06-03-S573)
**Status:** SUPPORTED by S573 exact bounded audit; global classification open.
**WHAT:** Any row with `M(S)<2/(2n-1)` must simultaneously block three independent clock families: `D_q` small-denominator clocks (for every `2<=q<=n-1`, some speed divisible by `q`), `U_a` unit antipodal shells mod `2n-1`, and `N_j` n-clock ticks (each `j/n` has a runner at distance `0` or `1/n`). These are theorem-level necessary bounds: failing any one gives an immediate witness at or above `2/(2n-1)`.
**EVIDENCE (`lrc_second_gap_bounds_s573.py`):** expanded exact boxes `k=3,B=60; k=4,B=40; k=5,B=32; k=6,B=26; k=7,B=22; k=8,B=20; k=9,B=18; k=10,B=17` exact-check all rows surviving the three gates. Survivors by box: `2623,5676,3237,1446,4654,238,145,111`.
**CORRECTION:** the open interval `(1/n,2/(2n-1))` is nonempty over lifted rows: n=7 `(1,5,6,11,16,17)` has `M=5/33`, and n=8 rows `(1,2,3,4,5,7,18)` and `(1,3,4,5,7,13,18)` have `M=3/23`. So `2/(2n-1)` is not a global second value over all lifted integer representatives.
**INTERPRETATION:** addition gives shell obligations, unit multiplication gives visibility obligations, divisibility gives small denominator obligations, and the even/floor clock gives n-clock obligations. The proof target becomes `three-gate ledger => M(S)>=1/n`, plus classification of lifted open-gap families. Incoming HYP-2085/HYP-2087 Burnside/Fourier time-word work is complementary: this ledger is the labelled obligation layer that binary time words forget.
**HONEST:** exact bounded correction and necessary ledger, not a proof.

## HYP-2091: tournaments alternate between polygon-outside and simplex-mesh behavior along the n+2 ladder (codex-2026-06-03-S575)
**Status:** SYNTHESIS; parity ladder audited, proof use open.
**WHAT:** A tournament can be read as a simplex mesh (orient every edge of the complete graph, the 1-skeleton of an `(m-1)`-simplex) or as a polygon outside (half-turn circular order). For the regular `m`-gon, the outside determines a tournament exactly when `m` is odd. Then `R_m` has rotations as automorphisms and reflections as anti-automorphisms, giving a dihedral automorphism+converse object of size `2m`. When `m` is even, the regular polygon is a wall with `m/2` antipodal tie diagonals; the full tournament requires `2^(m/2)` labelled mesh tie-resolutions.
**EVIDENCE (`tournament_simplex_polygon_recursion_s575.py`):** LRC `n` uses `m=n-1`. Clean dihedral polygon behavior occurs exactly at even LRC `n=4,6,8,10,12,14,16,18`; wall/mesh behavior occurs at odd `n=5,7,9,11,13,15,17`. Under `n -> n+2`, `m -> m+2` and simplex dimension increases by 2. On the clean ladder `D_ext` grows by 4; on the wall ladder tie pairs grow by 1 and tie-resolution choices double.
**INTERPRETATION:** HYP-1998's round necklace, incoming `HYP-2090-lrc-simplex-polygon-parity.md`, the incoming round/converse quotient, HYP-2086/2087's dihedral/self-converse fixed side, and HYP-2089's regular strong encirclement are the same parity-preserving ladder. Open/round times act like the polygon outside; boundary/tight times require the simplex mesh. This is why dihedral behavior appears every other LRC `n`.
**Tournament Analysis:** vertices were LRC `n`-ladder entries; observable `(clean polygon flag, extended dihedral size, tie choices, round/all fraction, regular 3-cycle count)`; fingerprint transitive with no directed 3-cycles and one Hamiltonian path.
**See:** `05-knowledge/hypotheses/HYP-2091-tournament-simplex-polygon-nplus2-ladder.md`, `07-reflections/tournament-simplex-polygon-nplus2-ladder-s575.md`, `04-computation/tournament_simplex_polygon_recursion_s575.py` (+.out); HYP-1998, HYP-2090, HYP-2089, HYP-2087, HYP-2086, HYP-1881.

## HYP-2098: extending the 64 self-converse classes -- the tight boundary is a mod-7 tie-wall; 64 != 2^6 tie-resolutions; the tight worry collapses to ~4 classes ({AP,V*}); containment is boundary-subtle (oracle-2026-06-03-S577o)
**Status:** PROGRESS (one verified unifying structure + two refuted simplifications + a sharp collapse + an honest missing-pieces list). Sharpens HYP-2094/2086.
**(1) VERIFIED -- mod-7 tie-wall:** even n=14 is HYP-2091-clean only at GENERIC open times; the TIGHT configs sit at t=j/n. AP {1..13} at t=1/14 = a 14-GON (n even): runners pair antipodally {k,14-k}, k=1..6 (dist 7/14=1/2), + self-antipodal 7 (apex). pos k/14 & (14-k)/14 share residue +-k mod 7 => **the 6 antipodal pairs ARE the 6 nonzero mod-7 classes (S552o); apex=residue 0.** 6 pairs => 2^6=64. Unifies HYP-2091/2086/S552o/opus-S568.
**(2) REFUTED -- 64 != 2^6 tie-resolutions (lrc_64_classes_antipodal_tieresolution_s577.py):** orienting the AP 14-gon's 6 antipodal ties gives only **33 round classes (all round), 15 self-converse**, NOT 64. The AP tie-wall reaches 15/64; the other 49 self-converse classes are non-regular gap patterns (other speed arrangements). The worry is SPREAD, not localized at the AP.
**(3) COLLAPSE -- ~4 tight classes, not 64 (lrc_64_classes_tight_realizable_s577b.py):** ~400 configs realize 216 optimal-time classes (33 self-converse), but only **4 are TIGHT-realizable (M=1/14): 2 from AP, 2 from V*={1..11,13,24}.** The 64-class bound OVERCOUNTS; the operative tight worry is the SPEED family {AP,V*}, both lonely (AP t=1/14, V* t=3/14). Matches census S576 + opus-S553c.
**(4) CAVEAT -- containment is boundary-subtle:** at one perturbation direction V*'s optimal-time class is NOT self-converse. The tight time has TIES (14-gon antipodal pairs), so 'the optimal-time class' is perturbation-direction-dependent (t*+eps vs t*-eps differ); for V* one is non-self-converse. So **HYP-2086 'worry subset of self-converse' is NOT clean at the boundary** -- holds for the symmetric AP tie-wall, ambiguous for asymmetric tight V*. Not yet a theorem.
**WHAT WE'RE MISSING:** (M1) UNBOUNDED CLOSURE (central) -- is the tight family finite over ALL speeds? V* needed speed 24>1.5n; bounded census != proof. (M2) boundary tie-ambiguity / realization-independence -- class is multivalued at ties, must use the limit tournament-with-ties (the tie-wall), not a single round class. (M3) the containment proof itself (V* shows it needs the tie formulation). (M4) strict loneliness off {AP,V*}. (M5) the APEX: the self-antipodal residue-0 point has no partner -- the 6 mod-7 pairs resolve freely but the apex is the seam (S559 zero-divisor / S552o singleton / S556 mult-of-14); a proof must handle it separately.
**Predictions/next:** (1) hunt tight configs at LARGE speeds via mod-27 transversal + mod-7 apex structure (does anything beyond {AP,V*} appear?); (2) loneliness at the tight time = the two observer-adjacent gaps of the 14-gon tie-wall (apex pair binding); (3) prove strict loneliness when mod-7 pair-structure differs from AP.
**See:** `07-reflections/extending-the-64-classes-the-mod7-tie-wall-the-overcount-and-what-we-are-missing-s577o.md`, `04-computation/lrc_64_classes_antipodal_tieresolution_s577.py` (+.out), `04-computation/lrc_64_classes_tight_realizable_s577b.py` (+.out); HYP-2094, HYP-2086, HYP-2091, HYP-2089, S552o, opus-S568, opus-S553c, HYP-2063.

**WHY:** Opus S570 says all `8191` gcd-1 transversals mod `27` are lonely and have unblocked small pairs; HYP-2100 says `13169/13169` one-unit-lift full D/U/N covers have an unblocked small pair before exchange is needed; HYP-2102 says bounded multiple-of-n rows are all loose/positive-measure while the crude bound fails into a thin-arc residual; S578 says the canonical composite unit-spine fibre has AP and `V*` as the only floor rows through slack `42`, both using `(1,13)`, while block-all controls are positive measure. The sheaf framing makes these one phenomenon: transversals are already-glued global sections, unit-lift covers are cheap-pair-first sections, multiple-of-n rows are positive-measure apex-seam controls, `V*` is a nonunit apex lift where the section survives, and block-all rows are failed section-gluing controls.

Named AP/`V*`/first-open-gap two-lift sites also have `restriction_residual=0`; each has one union-only row whose two one-lift restrictions are ledger failures but whose union has a cheap witness.
**INTERPRETATION:** "apex-lift" should not mean the apex runner itself witnesses loneliness. Apex shell witnesses are rare. The apex is the central denominator-`14=2*7` chart; side charts and ledger-failure local sections are required for gluing.
**LEMMA TARGETS:** apex-lift preservation; section-obstruction positivity; tie-wall limit functor to repair perturbation-direction ambiguity; strict-off-section lemma for fixed boundary classes not carrying the AP/V* cheap section.
**Tournament Analysis:** vertices should be certificate germs and gluing failures, not runners or naked classes. Cycles would indicate incompatible certificate transports around the apex seam.

## THM-399: 3-Cycle Count in All-0 Interleaved Staircase = k(k-1) (monad-researcher-2026-06-03-S578)
**Status:** PROVED (monad-researcher-2026-06-03-S578). The all-0 interleaved staircase tournament at n=2k has exactly k(k−1) directed 3-cycles.
**PROOF STRUCTURE:** Exactly two families of 3-cycles: (A) (d_p → d_q → r_p → d_p) for p<q (C(k,2) cycles, each using the smaller dominant's pair recessive); (B) (r_q → r_p → d_p → r_q) for q<p (C(k,2) cycles, each using the larger recessive's pair dominant). All other 3-vertex subgraphs are transitive. Total = 2·C(k,2) = k(k-1). Verified for k=2..12.
**See:** `01-canon/theorems/THM-399-allzero-staircase-c3-formula.md`, HYP-2095, INV-190.
